headline: CRML DELIVERS 100% TANBREEZ + $264.5M CASH — WORLD'S LARGEST UNDEVELOPED REE DEPOSIT SETS 2027 PRODUCTION ROADMAP
snippet: Critical Metals Corp (Nasdaq: CRML) announced November 11 that it has met all 2026 objectives — 100% ownership of Greenland's Tanbreez rare earth project, US$264.5 million in cash, and 194.2 million shares outstanding — and has published its 2027 development roadmap. With Greenland's government approving the Tanbreez mining and closure plan through 2050 covering 19 critical minerals including heavy rare earths dysprosium, terbium and yttrium, CRML is now the best-funded independent rare earth developer outside China.

headline: USAR CRATERS 11% ON $3M Q3 REVENUE — $141M OPERATING LOSS BUT FIRST COMMERCIAL NdFeB MAGNET SALES FROM OKLAHOMA
snippet: USA Rare Earth (Nasdaq: USAR) plunged 11% on November 10 after Q3 2026 revenue of just $3 million badly missed a consensus estimate near $14 million, with an operating loss of $141 million. The miss compounded Monday's CPI selloff, dragging Energy Fuels (UUUU) down 8% and MP Materials (MP) 5% in sympathy. Despite the miss, the company achieved its first commercial sales of neodymium-iron-boron block magnets from its Stillwater, Oklahoma facility and holds $1.2 billion in cash, with management guiding that Q4 mine revenue from Brazil alone will exceed the entire first-nine-months total.

headline: NORTHWEST COPPER HITS 61.9M AT 1.01% CuEq AT KWANIKA NORTH PIT EXTENSION — BC PORPHYRY ZONE GROWS FROM 39M DEPTH
snippet: NorthWest Copper (TSX-V: NWST) reported 61.9 metres grading 0.37% copper and 0.58 g/t gold (1.01% CuEq) starting from just 39 metres depth in the North Pit Extension Zone at its Kwanika porphyry copper-gold project in north-central British Columbia, extending a mineralized corridor the company is advancing toward a development study alongside its Stardust deposit.

headline: COPPER BOUNCES 1.8% AS AI SENTIMENT RECOVERS AND SHFE STOCKS HIT 3-YEAR LOW — PHYSICAL TIGHTNESS UNDERPINS REBOUND
snippet: Copper gained approximately 1.8% Wednesday to US$6.35/lb on Comex as AI-linked technology stocks rebounded from Monday's CPI selloff, lifting broader risk appetite, while SHFE-monitored warehouse inventories continued their steep decline — down over 75% in the past six months — confirming genuine physical tightness inside China even as macro headwinds from US rate-hike expectations weigh on futures prices.

headline: MINSUD DRILLS 186M AT 0.48% COPPER, 0.18 G/T GOLD, 10.1 G/T SILVER TO END OF HOLE — OPEN-ENDED PORPHYRY, ARGENTINA
snippet: Minsud Resources (TSX-V: MSA) reported hole CHDH26-174 at its Chita Valley porphyry project in Argentina returned 186 metres grading 0.48% copper, 0.18 g/t gold and 10.1 g/t silver, confirming linked high-grade polymetallic breccias across a porphyry copper-molybdenum-gold-silver centre. The hole was stopped at 186 metres due to drill equipment limitations with mineralization open at depth, and a follow-up deeper hole is being planned to test the full extent of the system.

headline: BUNKER HILL + SILVER47 CLOSE MERGER — 388M AgEq OZ 'MADE IN AMERICA' SILVER CO, BOARD UPDATE ISSUED NOV 11
snippet: Bunker Hill Mining completed its merger with Silver47 Exploration on November 6, 2026, with a board composition update issued November 11, creating a U.S.-focused silver producer with 80 million measured and indicated ounces plus 308 million inferred ounces of silver equivalent across four wholly domestic projects — Bunker Hill's producing Idaho mine and Silver47's Red Mountain (Alaska), Hughes (Nevada) and Mogollon (New Mexico). The combined entity will trade as Bunker Hill Silver Corp. on the TSX, with 2026 production guidance near 980,000 AgEq oz, targeting 2.5 million oz by 2027.

headline: BARRICK BEATS Q3 ESTIMATES AS GOLD PRODUCTION RECOVERS — 2026 ANNUAL GUIDANCE HELD DESPITE GOLD'S NOV SLIDE
snippet: Barrick Mining beat Q3 2026 earnings consensus on November 9 as gold production improved quarter-over-quarter and the company maintained its full-year 2026 guidance, reinforcing the message from the broader gold producer earnings season that miners are capitalizing on record realized gold prices well above $4,000 per ounce. The report came days after Barrick filed to spin out its North American assets as American Barrick Gold Corp (NYSE: ABGC) in what could be a $42 billion IPO.

headline: GOLD MINERS ROSE WHILE SPOT FELL MONDAY — RARE BULLISH DIVERGENCE THAT OFTEN SIGNALS REAL CAPITULATION BOTTOMS
snippet: On Monday's CPI-shock selloff, gold equities did something unusual: they held steady or rose even as spot gold fell sharply, a bullish divergence that analysts read as capitulation finishing in the equity market. Gold mining stocks typically amplify spot moves 2-3x to the downside, so diverging upward during a metal decline often signals that forced sellers have exhausted supply and equity-only buyers are stepping in at the discount.

headline: JUNIOR MINERS RAISED $18B IN H1 2026 — COPPER, GOLD, URANIUM CAPTURED CAPITAL AS LITHIUM/NICKEL EXPLORATION COOLS
snippet: An industry analysis finds that junior mining raised a record US$18 billion in the first half of 2026, but capital is concentrating in copper, gold and uranium rather than battery metals — lithium and nickel projects face tighter financing without demonstrated low-cost production. The analysis identifies funded, multi-year drill programs in stable jurisdictions as the principal beneficiaries, while early-stage lithium and nickel explorers are largely shut out of equity markets.

headline: SUPER COPPER'S MAIDEN DRILL: 4-FOR-4 AT EL ALTO IN CHILE'S ATACAMA — ALL HOLES HIT STRUCTURALLY HOSTED COPPER
snippet: Super Copper Corp. reported its maiden drill program at the El Alto target in Chile's Atacama Region confirmed copper mineralization in all four assayed holes, with structurally hosted copper intersected across the entire target area. The 4-for-4 success rate validates the geological model at an early-stage copper discovery in one of the world's premier copper provinces, though the company notes that advancing the program will require substantial additional capital.
